description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved Hong Kong bakery staple, despite containing no pineapple fruit. These sweet buns feature a soft, fluffy interior crowned with a crispy, crumbly, sugary crust that resembles the skin of a pineapple. Enjoy them warm for a delightful breakfast or snack.

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 250g all-purpose flour, 40g granulated sugar, instant dry yeast, and salt. Add warm milk and the beaten egg for the bun dough. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then add the softened unsalted butter. Knead on a lightly floured surface or with a stand mixer for 10-15 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let it proof in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is proofing, prepare the topping. In a separate bowl, cream together 70g softened unsalted butter and 60g confectioners' sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk until well combined. In another small bowl, whisk together 120g all-purpose flour, custard powder, milk powder, and baking powder. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, alternating with evaporated milk, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap the topping dough in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the Bun Dough
instructions.text: Once the bun dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release the air. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and divide it into 8 equal portions (about 60-70g each). Roll each portion into a smooth, round ball. Place the shaped dough balls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them.

instructions.title: Form and Apply the Topping
instructions.text: Remove the chilled topping dough from the refrigerator. Divide it into 8 equal portions. On a piece of plastic wrap or between two sheets of parchment paper, flatten each topping portion into a thin disc, about 3-4 inches (7-10 cm) in diameter. Carefully peel one topping disc and drape it over a bun dough ball, gently pressing it down to adhere and cover about two-thirds of the bun's surface, leaving the bottom uncovered.

instructions.title: Second Proof and Egg Wash
instructions.text: Once all buns are topped, cover the baking sheet loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel. Let the buns proof again in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Preheat your oven to 350F (175C). Just before baking, gently brush the topping of each bun with the beaten egg wash for a golden sheen.

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Bake the pineapple buns in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy, and the buns are cooked through. The internal temperature of the bun should reach 200-210F (93-99C). Remove from the oven and transfer to a wire rack to cool slightly. Serve warm for the best texture and flavor.

tips: For an extra crispy topping, ensure your butter for the topping is well-creamed and the topping dough is chilled before shaping.
If you cant find custard powder, you can omit it, but it contributes to the signature color and a subtle flavor. You can also substitute with a small amount of cornstarch for texture.

Pineapple buns are best enjoyed fresh and warm. If storing, keep them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for longer storage. Reheat in a toaster oven or microwave.
article:
Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao) is more than just a pastry; it's a culinary icon, a warm hug in edible form, and a staple of Chinese bakeries worldwide. Originating from Hong Kong, this beloved bun, despite its name, contains no pineapple at all. Instead, it earns its moniker from the distinctive, cracked, golden-brown topping that resembles the skin of a pineapple. Beneath this sweet, crumbly crust lies a pillowy soft, slightly sweet milk bread, creating a delightful contrast of textures and flavors that has captivated generations.

Whether you're a seasoned baker or a curious food enthusiast, the journey of creating Bo Lo Bao from scratch is incredibly rewarding. This article will delve into the history and appeal of this famous pastry, guide you through a detailed Pineapple Bun Recipe, and provide expert tips to ensure your homemade buns are nothing short of perfection. Get ready to fill your kitchen with the irresistible aroma of freshly baked Chinese goodness!

## What is Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

Bo Lo Bao, or Pineapple Bun, is a quintessential item found in Hong Kong-style bakeries, dim sum restaurants, and cha chaan tengs (Hong Kong-style diners). Its fame stems from its unique dual texture: a tender, slightly sweet bread base and a sugary, crispy, cookie-like topping. The bread itself is typically enriched with milk and egg, resulting in a light, fluffy crumb that practically melts in your mouth.

The "pineapple" element refers solely to the appearance of the topping. Made from a mixture of flour, sugar, butter, and egg, this topping is carefully spread over the proofed bread dough before baking. As it bakes, the topping expands and cracks, forming a beautiful, checkered pattern reminiscent of a pineapple's rough exterior. This delightful contrast between the soft interior and crunchy exterior is what makes the Pineapple Bun so incredibly addictive and a must-try for anyone exploring Chinese baking. It's often enjoyed for breakfast, as a snack with milk tea, or as a comforting treat any time of day.

## Ingredients for Homemade Pineapple Buns

Crafting the perfect Pineapple Bun requires attention to detail and quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need for this fulfilling Pineapple Bun Recipe:

**For the Bread Dough:**
*   **Bread Flour:** High protein content is essential for a chewy, elastic crumb.
*   **Granulated Sugar:** Sweetens the dough and aids yeast activation.
*   **Salt:** Balances flavors and strengthens gluten.
*   **Instant Dry Yeast:** For leavening and that characteristic bread aroma.
*   **Warm Milk:** Activates the yeast and provides moisture.
*   **Large Egg:** Adds richness, color, and helps bind the dough.
*   **Unsalted Butter (softened):** Contributes tenderness and flavor.

**For the Pineapple Topping (Bo Lo Bao Topping):**
*   **All-Purpose Flour:** The base for the crispy topping.
*   **Powdered Sugar:** Creates a fine, tender crumb.
*   **Unsalted Butter (cold, cubed):** Crucial for flakiness and crispness.
*   **Large Egg Yolk:** Adds richness, color, and binds the topping.
*   **Evaporated Milk (or whole milk):** For moisture and a slightly creamy flavor.
*   **Baking Powder (optional):** A pinch can enhance the topping's crispness and crackle.

**For Egg Wash (for topping):**
*   **Egg Yolk mixed with a splash of milk:** For a golden, shiny finish.

Ensuring your butter is cold for the topping and softened for the dough is key to achieving the right textures.

## How to Make Pineapple Buns: Step-by-Step Guide

This comprehensive Pineapple Bun Recipe will guide you through the process, from kneading the dough to baking golden perfection.

**Part 1: Making the Bread Dough**
1.  **Activate Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine warm milk, a tablespoon of sugar, and instant yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Combine Dry Ingredients:** In a separate bowl, whisk together bread flour, remaining sugar, and salt.
3.  **Mix Dough:** Add the activated yeast mixture and the egg to the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or stand mixer (with a dough hook) until a shaggy dough forms.
4.  **Knead:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Alternatively, knead in a stand mixer on medium speed for 8-10 minutes.
5.  **Add Butter:** Gradually incorporate the softened butter, kneading until fully absorbed and the dough is very smooth and pliable. It should pass the "windowpane test" (stretch a small piece thinly without tearing).
6.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
7.  **Divide and Shape:** Gently punch down the dough to release air. Divide it into 8-10 equal pieces (around 60-70g each). Shape each piece into a smooth, round ball.
8.  **Second Rise (Proofing):** Arrange the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them rise for another 45-60 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.

**Part 2: Making the Pineapple Topping**
1.  **Cream Butter and Sugar:** In a medium bowl, cream together the cold, cubed butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
2.  **Add Wet Ingredients:** Beat in the egg yolk and evaporated milk until well combined.
3.  **Incorporate Dry:** Sift in the all-purpose flour (and baking powder, if using). Mix gently with a spatula or your hands until just combined and a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
4.  **Chill:** Flatten the topping dough into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. This makes it easier to handle.

**Part 3: Assembly and Baking**
1.  **Prepare Topping:** Remove the chilled topping dough. Divide it into the same number of pieces as your bread buns. Roll each piece into a thin circle (about 4-5 inches in diameter) on a lightly floured surface or between two sheets of parchment paper.
2.  **Apply Topping:** Carefully drape a circle of topping over each proofed bread bun. Gently press the edges down to secure it, but avoid compressing the bun itself.
3.  **Egg Wash & Score:** Brush the topping with the egg yolk wash. Using a knife or dough scraper, lightly score a crisscross pattern on the topping of each bun. This enhances the pineapple-like appearance.
4.  **Bake:** Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake the Pineapple Buns for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the buns are cooked through.
5.  **Cool:** Transfer the baked buns to a wire rack to cool slightly. This is a classic Pineapple Bun Recipe that yields authentic results.

## Tips for the Perfect Crispy Topping

The signature crispy, crumbly topping is what sets Bo Lo Bao apart. Here are some essential tips to master this crucial component of your Pineapple Bun Recipe:

*   **Cold Butter is Key:** For the topping, always use very cold, cubed butter. This helps create pockets of steam during baking, leading to a flakier, crispier texture.
*   **Don't Overmix the Topping:** Overmixing develops gluten in the flour, which can make the topping tough instead of crumbly. Mix just until combined.
*   **Chill the Topping Dough:** Chilling the topping makes it firmer and much easier to roll out thinly without it sticking or tearing. It also prevents the butter from melting too quickly when it hits the warm bread dough.
*   **Roll Evenly and Thinly:** Aim for a consistent thickness when rolling out the topping. Too thick, and it might be heavy; too thin, and it could tear easily.
*   **Gentle Handling:** When placing the topping over the proofed buns, be gentle. You don't want to deflate the beautifully risen dough.
*   **Egg Wash for Shine:** The egg yolk wash not only gives a beautiful golden color but also helps create that desirable slight sheen on the baked topping.
*   **Score Lightly:** The scoring is mostly for aesthetics. Don't cut too deep into the bread dough, just enough to mark the topping.

Mastering these tips is key to perfecting your homemade Pineapple Bun Recipe.

## Serving and Storage Suggestions

Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed warm, fresh from the oven, when the contrast between the crispy topping and soft bread is at its peak.

**Serving Suggestions:**
*   **Classic Buttered Bo Lo Bao (Bo Lo Yau):** Slice the warm bun horizontally and insert a thick slab of cold, unsalted butter. The butter melts into the warm bread, creating a rich, decadent treat.
*   **With Hot Beverages:** Pair it with a cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea, coffee, or hot lemon tea for a traditional experience.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** It's a perfect grab-and-go breakfast or a comforting afternoon snack.

**Storage:**
*   **Room Temperature:** Store leftover buns in an airtight container at room temperature for 1-2 days. The topping may soften slightly over time.
*   **Reheating:** To revive the crispness of the topping and softness of the bread, reheat the buns in a preheated oven at 300°F (150°C) for 5-10 minutes, or until warmed through. A quick zap in the microwave will warm them, but the topping won't be as crispy.
*   **Freezing:** For longer storage, wrap individual buns tightly in plastic wrap, then place them in a freezer-safe bag. They can be frozen for up to 1 month. Reheat directly from frozen in a preheated oven until warm.

## Pineapple Bun Variations

While the traditional approach of our Pineapple Bun Recipe is wonderful, there are many delightful variations to explore:

*   **Filled Pineapple Buns:** Many bakeries offer Pineapple Buns with various fillings. Popular choices include:
    *   **Custard:** A creamy, sweet egg custard.
    *   **Red Bean Paste:** A sweet, earthy paste made from adzuki beans.
    *   **Char Siu (BBQ Pork):** A savory and sweet filling for a delightful contrast.
    *   **Ham and Egg:** A common breakfast-style filling.
*   **Bo Lo Yau (Pineapple Bun with Butter):** As mentioned, this is a classic where a slice of cold butter is inserted into the warm bun just before serving.
*   **Mini Pineapple Buns:** Smaller versions, perfect for parties or sampling multiple flavors.
*   **Flavored Toppings:** Some variations might include matcha powder, cocoa powder, or even a hint of coffee in the topping for different flavor profiles.

Don't hesitate to experiment with the fillings and flavors once you've mastered the basic Pineapple Bun Recipe.

Making Pineapple Buns at home is a truly rewarding experience, allowing you to savor the fresh aroma and irresistible taste of this iconic Chinese pastry. From the satisfying process of kneading the dough to the joy of biting into a warm, crispy-topped bun, every step is a delight. Armed with this comprehensive Pineapple Bun Recipe and our expert tips, you're ready to create your own batch of delicious Bo Lo Bao and share a taste of Hong Kong's culinary heritage with your loved ones. Happy baking!
